summary: Paper W3021197939 (TRIC: A Thermal Resistance and Impedance Calculator for Electronic Packages) describes a compact thermal model extraction tool for eTQFP, eLQFP, pLQFP, eQFN, and related packages. Figure 6 on page 7 presents transient thermal impedance ZTHJA versus time for a 10×10 mm² eTQFP with 6×6 mm² epad under 1 W power step, parameterized across die sizes (2×2 to 5×5 mm²). The scenario is fundamentally illustrative of the TRIC methodology rather than a reproducible experimental validation dataset. The paper validates TRIC against FloTHERM v12.2 with reported <3% discrepancy and 15–20× CPU speedup, but does not provide sufficient implementation detail (mesh dimensions, material properties, full boundary condition specifications, or code/data repositories) to enable independent replication. Studio cannot execute this scenario because: (1) the experiment type is declared as custom_2d_steady but lacks floorplan blocks and power_w mapping required for instantiation; (2) the scenario describes a 3D transient thermal simulation (transient time-domain response from 10⁻⁵ s to 10³ s), contradicting the steady-state label; (3) essential input parameters such as die thickness, detailed material properties, and mesh discretization are missing or stated only in context of other package families; (4) no digital artifact (source code, CAD, or supplementary data) is linked or available for cross-validation. The scenario is classified as not_2d_applicable because thermal packaging analysis in TRIC inherently requires 3D representation of die, epad, mold, leads, and board geometry with full spatial detail; 2D approximations are explicitly not supported by the tool's architecture.
limitations: Experiment metadata declares custom_2d_steady type but provides neither floorplan blocks nor power_w object; Studio input validation gate fails immediately.
Scenario describes transient 3D thermal impedance evolution (time-dependent heat diffusion from 10⁻⁵ s to 10³ s), incompatible with steady-state 2D assumption; temporal regime mismatch.

Die thickness for Figure 6 not explicitly stated; paper mentions 100, 280, 375, 580 µm variants for eLQFP but does not specify which applies to the eTQFP scenario, preventing exact geometry reconstruction.
Material thermal conductivity and volumetric heat capacity values (die, attach, epad, mold, board, leads) not tabulated; only weighted-average aggregates and qualitative descriptions provided.
Mesh discretization parameters (nx, ny, nz grid points, timestep nt) not disclosed; convergence criterion stated as ≤0.1% but reference geometry and validation mesh details absent.

TRIC source code, executable, mesh files, and supplementary material repository not linked or publicly accessible; validation against FloTHERM v12.2 relies on internal comparisons with no external reproduction pathway.
Boundary conditions cited to JEDEC JESD51-12 but full specification (convective heat transfer coefficients, radiation, symmetry planes, board extent) not reproduced in paper.
FloTHERM v12.2 setup parameters (mesh style, iterative solver tolerances, convergence criteria) not detailed; ~3% discrepancy attributed to mesh differences without quantitative reconciliation.

Figure 6 uses artificial instantaneous 1 W power step at t=0, not representative of realistic semiconductor workloads; no dynamic power profile, clock frequency, or die-level thermal coupling documented.

Package geometry simplified to Manhattan rectangular parallelepipeds with adiabatic symmetry planes; pLQFP die position shifts and multi-source layouts require ad-hoc projection basis adaptation not detailed for eTQFP.

TRIC is a model extraction and parameterization tool, not a direct 3D thermal solver; Figure 6 impedance curves are outputs of model-order reduction (MOR) applied to reduced-order parametric detailed thermal models (pDTMs), not raw FV solutions.

Steady-state junction-to-ambient thermal resistance ϑJA derived from compact thermal network; does not isolate individual thermal path contributions (lead, epad, mold) or enable localized thermal gradient analysis.
No uncertainty quantification for digitized impedance values from Figure 6 plot; estimated ±0.5 K/W margin assumes linear plot resolution but systematic reading error unvalidated.
Physical mismatch: simplified Manhattan geometry with weighted-average material properties vs. actual lead profiles, die attach thickness variation, and epad solder mask details.
Physical mismatch: idealized JEDEC boundary conditions (step function heat transfer coefficient) vs. realistic thermal interface material (TIM) behavior and board thermal resistance distribution.
A custom experiment needs 1–128 blocks and a power_w object
